pipeline.name: clearfelt-writing-write
pipeline.config: Read human_score_threshold, max_iterations, and length from clearfelt-writing.config.md, layered under any ~/.clearfelt-writing/settings.md global override and any .clearfelt-writing/domain.md preferred_length project override. Do not hardcode these values here; the config files are the single source of truth.

pass.name: seed_and_interview
pass.goal: Resolve what's actually being written: the seed, its structure, and how long the result should be, before generating anything.

steps.step: Resolve the seed: a file path if one was given, or the text pasted directly into the request. If neither is present, ask for one plainly; never invent a topic from nothing.
This whole pipeline operates under writing.md's doctrine and voice.md's precedence rule, same as prompts/audit_loop.xml. Both apply throughout every pass below, not just here.

Check for .clearfelt-writing/voice-profile.md (or .clearfelt-writing/voices/<name>.md in multi-voice mode). If present, read it and note preferred vocabulary, sentence rhythm notes, and non-negotiables, same as rewrite's Pass 1. If its first non-blank line is "extends: <base-name>" (see docs/decisions/0021), also read .clearfelt-writing/voices/<base-name>.md and apply both, per section: list-type sections (words to keep/avoid, non-negotiables) union, this file's entries add to the base's, never replace them; sentence rhythm uses this file's own text if it states one, otherwise the base's. The base file is never itself expected to have its own extends: line; if it does, that is a config error, not something to resolve by guessing, say so and stop rather than picking a direction. If absent, mention once that /clearfelt-writing setup can build one, then continue with bundled defaults; never block on it.

Check .clearfelt-writing/domain.md for mode and risk_tier, same meaning as in rewrite's Pass 1: mode is context for later judgment calls, risk_tier: sensitive forces the confirm-before-write gate on regardless of clearfelt-writing.config.md or a saved global preference (write has no independent confirmation setting, it reuses rewrite.require_confirmation, see clearfelt-writing.config.md's Write section).

Ask a short interview, at most 4 questions, each through the AskUserQuestion wizard pattern reference/setup.md uses: concrete example options plus Other, one question per turn, never a bare open text prompt. Cover format (post, article, email, README section, ...), target audience, and any point the seed doesn't state but the piece must hit. Skip a question outright if .clearfelt-writing/domain.md already answers it (format and audience are often domain-level, not per-draft); do not re-ask what's already resolved.

Resolve the length to run at, in this order: .clearfelt-writing/domain.md's preferred_length field (project-level, if present) beats ~/.clearfelt-writing/settings.md's length/write.ask_length (global save, if present) beats clearfelt-writing.config.md's shipped default (write.ask_length: true means ask).

If asking (no resolved preference): present the three-tier table (short, medium, long; see reference/write.md for what each targets) following reference/format/write.md's "Length question template". After the user picks, ask a second, separate question: save this choice, and if so, globally (writes to ~/.clearfelt-writing/settings.md) or just for this project (writes preferred_length to .clearfelt-writing/domain.md, creating it from templates/domain.example.md if needed)? Do not save anything without this explicit second answer.
If not asking (a resolved preference already exists): state which length is being used and why (saved preference, project- or global-scoped), and mention how to change it. Proceed without blocking.

Record the seed's own factual payload: any claim, number, name, date, or quote it already states. These, plus anything a genuine interview answer adds, are the only facts the draft is allowed to contain; see the no-fabrication reinterpretation in reference/write.md.

Resolve any active constraints (see reference/rewrite.md's "Constraints", reused as-is by write): an explicit --constraints <name> naming a .clearfelt-writing/constraints/<name>.md file, and/or inline --max-chars/--max-words/--must-contain/--must-not-contain given with the request. Carry these into Pass 2, where they matter more than in rewrite: there's no existing draft whose length is already close, so a hard ceiling has to be a generation target from the very first draft, not a check applied afterward. No constraints is the common case, proceed without them.

pass.name: draft_from_seed
pass.goal: Generate a first full draft from the seed and interview answers, at the resolved length.

steps.step: Write a complete draft at the resolved length tier's target word count, in the format and for the audience resolved in Pass 1. If Pass 1 resolved a max_chars/max_words constraint, that ceiling governs over the length tier's target where the two conflict, draft to the constraint, not past it.
The seed's stated position is load-bearing: the draft must not soften, reverse, or omit the seed's actual claim. Expand and support it, don't dilute it.

No-fabrication rule, write's version: never introduce a name, date, statistic, or quote that isn't in the seed or an interview answer. Connective tissue, examples, and structure are expected to be new, that is the point of this command; a fact is not.
Apply voice-profile preferences and contractions where natural, same as rewrite's scrub pass, from the first draft onward, not as a later cleanup step.

On a re-entry into this pass from the loop below, treat this as a rewrite of the current candidate draft, not a fresh draft from the seed: apply the same scrub-slop scope escalation rewrite's Pass 2 uses (structural variation, sentence-length variety, addressing reference/audit.md's qualitative signals), still bounded by the no-fabrication rule above. If the prior check.mjs run in Pass 3 failed on a constraint, fixing that (trim to fit, add the required text, remove the forbidden one) takes priority over further slop-scrubbing in this re-entry.

pass.name: score_and_preserve_evaluation
pass.goal: Score the current draft, verify its facts against the seed in code, and decide whether another draft pass is needed.

steps.step: Write the current candidate draft to .clearfelt-writing/candidate.md (creating .clearfelt-writing/ if needed; gitignored, machine-written scratch state).

If this draft deliberately repeats a phrase as a hook/CTA callback or anaphora (a rhetorical device, not filler), pass it to the score: node scripts/detect.mjs --mode score .clearfelt-writing/candidate.md --exempt-repetition "<the repeated phrase>" (repeatable for more than one). Otherwise run without the flag. See docs/decisions/0022: the tool never guesses which repetition was intentional, only exempts what's explicitly declared, so declare only a phrase actually repeated on purpose, not every repeated word.
Compare the returned score against human_score_threshold.

Write the seed text (the seed file's content, or the pasted seed text, plus every interview answer as plain lines) to .clearfelt-writing/seed.md, then run: node scripts/check.mjs --before .clearfelt-writing/seed.md --after .clearfelt-writing/candidate.md [any constraint flags resolved in Pass 1] Read the JSON verdict. A locked-span mismatch is not expected here (a fresh seed rarely has lock markers) but is still handled identically to rewrite's Pass 3 if one is present. Treat the fingerprint's dropped list as expected noise, the seed is short by design, most of what a full draft "drops" relative to it never existed as a fact to preserve. Treat the added list as the one that matters: a genuinely new number, date, name, or quote not traceable to the seed or an interview answer means a real fabrication risk, not just a stylistic difference; if check.hard_fail_on_added_fact is true, this blocks the write exactly as it would for rewrite; if false (the default), it carries forward into the confirmation view as a disclosed warning, see reference/format/write.md's "Preservation check block". A max_chars/max_words overshoot always blocks (same as rewrite), regardless of hard_fail_configured; a must_contain/must_not_contain miss blocks under check.hard_fail_on_constraint_violation (on by default).

loop.condition: score < human_score_threshold or (check_verdict == 'fail' and hard_fail_configured) or length_constraint_exceeded

pass.loop: Re-run pass 2 with the "re-entry" instruction above. If max_iterations is reached without clearing the threshold or resolving a check.mjs failure, stop and report the final score and any unresolved preservation violation honestly rather than looping forever.
